author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty by address
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces, the paged page and the reinstated machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive. A blank specialty narrows nothing. No page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Given no specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as today (every veterinarian; the page paged five at a time).
Given /vets.html?specialty=<name> or /vets?specialty=<name>, only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, each shown with all of their specialties.
A specialty differing from a held one only by letter case matches on both surfaces (e.g. SURGERY matches surgery).
Only a whole specialty name matches: a prefix such as surg matches no veterinarian on either surface.
A specialty no veterinarian holds, including an unknown name, yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document carrying an empty veterinarian list.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if the parameter were absent on both surfaces.
On /vets.html, pagination applies to the narrowed list: total pages and page content count only matching veterinarians.
On /vets.html, every pagination link of a narrowed page carries the same specialty parameter, so filtered pages stay navigable.
A veterinarian holding no specialty is never matched, including by specialty=none, the word the page shows in its place.
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty (owner: may come as a follow-up request)
Filtering by more than one specialty, or by any attribute other than specialty
Reusing or reinstating the withdrawn ID REQ-VET-002
notes: Unfiltered behavior on both surfaces is already covered by the existing tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList; they stay green and owe no new name. REQ-VET-003 is the fresh requirement the owner asked for: it reinstates the machine-readable list as a supported surface, and the specialty filter is its first capability. The page-surface filter is tagged to the same ID so the capability stays one requirement. Decided as the narrowest reading, owner absent: a narrowed page lists each matching veterinarian with all their specialties, and the machine-readable list stays unpaged. Open, recorded in PRD Open Questions: whether a name with surrounding spaces (e.g. ' surgery ') matches. The slice promises nothing for it, and no test is owed. For system-design-expert: the Known Defects row in system-design.md saying the machine-readable route serves no requirement, and the Contracts rows for Vets/VetController, are now stale (REQ-VET-003). The ADR index in docs/adr/README.md lacks the new non-goal ADR, which is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Minor adjustment of the vet feature package (system-design.md § Contracts rows Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController; § Scale and Load new row). The filter follows the owner-search precedent: OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith is a paged Spring Data derived query, and OwnerController normalizes the blank value before calling it (basis: grep of OwnerRepository.java:45 and OwnerController.java:98-136; IDE oracle not connected, the weaker basis). VetRepository gains derived queries narrowing by Specialty name, one paged and one whole, e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and the Collection overload. The match is the query predicate: whole name, case-insensitive, Distinct so no veterinarian appears twice (specialties.name is not unique in the schemas). Veterinarians without a specialty never join, so specialty=none matches nobody. VetController binds an optional String specialty on both routes; a blank value (no text after hasText) routes to today's unfiltered calls unchanged. That normalization is binding per architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; no other rule lands in the controller. A non-blank value reaches the query unchanged: no strip, since surrounding spaces are a PRD open question the slice promises nothing on. The page model gains the normalized specialty only when filtered, and vetList.html carries it on every pagination link. Unfiltered output (page, links, JSON) stays byte-for-byte as today.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html and GET /vets: the new input binds to a request-scoped optional String request parameter named specialty; no persisted type is bound.

Double, repository boundary for the matching semantics (case, prefix, unknown name, none, blank-as-absent, narrowed totals): the real VetRepository against the seeded H2 database, driven through MockMvc in a new full-context test class (@SpringBootTest with MockMvc auto-configuration) in the vet test package. Test names: theVetPageShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetPageShouldMatchTheWholeSpecialtyNameIgnoringCaseButNotAPrefix, theVetPageShouldShowAnEmptyListForASpecialtyNoVetHolds, theVetPageShouldTreatAnEmptyOrBlankSpecialtyAsAbsent, theVetPageShouldPaginateTheNarrowedListOnly, theVetPageShouldNotMatchVetsWithoutSpecialtyWhenFilteredByNone, and the four theVetList* names. A stub would re-implement the predicate under test; seed data suffices (surgery: Linda Douglas, Rafael Ortega; radiology: Helen Leary, Henry Stevens; James Carter and Sharon Jenkins hold none; six vets give two unfiltered pages against one narrowed page). Linda Douglas also holds dentistry, which proves each match keeps all its specialties.

Double, repository boundary for theVetPagePaginationLinksShouldCarryTheSpecialty only: the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub in VetControllerTests (@WebMvcTest, MockMvc as the sanctioned transport), returning a narrowed page whose total exceeds one page. Reason: the seed holds no Specialty with more than five veterinarians, and the test asserts link rendering, not matching; testing-principles § Mocking Policy tolerates the class's existing stub.
Framework transport: MockMvc in both classes, per CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy.

patterns.description: paged Spring Data derived query as the search predicate
controller normalizes an absent or blank search value before querying (binding, not a business rule)
existing vet pagination helper; page size stays the local five

risks.risk: Veterinarian directory path, system-design.md § Scale and Load row 'Veterinarian directory, whole or narrowed by Specialty': a fetch join on the filter would truncate each veterinarian's specialties to the matched one.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form per the row: a derived query joining the Specialty in the predicate only, with the eager collection loaded separately; the integration test asserts Linda Douglas lists both surgery and dentistry.

risks.risk: Cache growth from request-chosen keys (system-design.md § Threat Model row 'Cache growth from request-chosen keys'; § Scale and Load Limits): the vets cache has no size limit, so @Cacheable on a narrowed query would admit one entry per caller-chosen string.
risks.mitigation: The narrowed query methods carry no @Cacheable; only the existing unfiltered reads stay cached.

risks.risk: Request text in template links (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external input; system-design.md § Threat Model row 'Request text reaching a template expression or link'): the existing links use __${...}__ preprocessing and string concatenation, and copying that shape for specialty is an expression-injection vector.
risks.mitigation: Build every pagination link with link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, rendered without the specialty parameter when unfiltered. The request value never enters __...__ preprocessing or a concatenated URL.

risks.risk: Injection into data access (security-principles § Language Realization, injection row).
risks.mitigation: Derived query only; no JPQL or SQL text built from the value.

notes: Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md Contracts rows Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController now cite REQ-VET-003 and record the placement (match in the repository query, blank-as-absent in controller binding). Security Context inputs and outputs are updated. Two Threat Model rows are added (link encoding, cache keys). docs/adr/README.md index gains the 2026-11-05 non-goal ADR row. No new architectural ADR: the slice reuses the owner-search pattern, and the uncached-narrowed-read choice is one clause on the VetRepository row. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Observation outside this slice, unconfirmed and not recorded as a defect: ownersList.html pagination links also drop the lastName search value, so paging a filtered owner search loses the filter. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied Specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable)` and `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` (VetRepository.java, added in the diff), which bind it as a parameter; `grep -F -e '@Query' -e 'createQuery' -e 'nativeQuery' src/main/java` returns only the pre-existing PetTypeRepository.java:36 `@Query("SELECT ptype FROM PetType ptype ORDER BY ptype.name")`, so no concatenated query text was added.

Template-expression and XSS safety: the change removes the four `__${...}__` preprocessing hrefs from vetList.html and replaces them with link-expression parameters (vetList.html:30 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}` and lines 35, 40, 45, 50 alike), so the echoed Specialty is URL-encoded and attribute-escaped and never enters preprocessing; `grep -n -F -e 'utext'` on the template finds no unescaped output, and the Specialty is echoed nowhere else on the page. VetControllerTests asserts the encoding with `oral & dental` -> `oral%20%26%20dental`. Remaining `__${` uses in fragments/ and ownerDetails.html are pre-existing and carry no request-derived text.

Resource growth: narrowed reads are not annotated `@Cacheable`, so a caller-chosen Specialty adds no entry to the unbounded `vets` cache; only the pre-existing unfiltered `findAll` reads stay cached (VetRepository.java diff).

Input validation at the boundary: the optional `specialty` @RequestParam is a plain String, blank treated as absent via `StringUtils::hasText`; no request-bound object, no mass-assignment surface, no new binder, and no removed or weakened check in the diff.

Exposed surface: no new route; both existing GET routes `/vets.html` and `/vets` gain one read-only query parameter, matching the threat-model rows added to docs/system-design.md (link-expression encoding, cache bypass). No mutation, no management-endpoint change.
Secrets: the diff adds no credential, token, password, key, or connection string (read of the full changeset).

Supply chain: build.gradle and gradle/ are unchanged (`git status --short build.gradle gradle/` empty). `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.2, Jackson databind (tools.jackson) 3.1.7, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Hibernate 7.4.13.Final; no NVD scan ran, a standing gap listed in docs/security-principles.md § Standing Gaps.

approved_aspects: Template-expression safety of the new fragment: the request-supplied Specialty reaches markup only inside link-expression parameters, pageLink.html:8 `th:href="${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=${target})} : @{/vets.html(page=${target},specialty=${specialty})}"`, so it is URL-encoded and attribute-escaped and never enters preprocessing or a concatenated URL, matching docs/system-design.md:193. The one preprocessing use the fix adds, pageLink.html:9 `#{__${titleKey}__}`, takes only template literals: `grep -rn -F -e 'pageLink' src/main/resources/templates src/main/java` finds five callers, all in vetList.html (lines 31, 38, 44, 50, 56), passing `null`, 'first', 'previous', 'next', 'last'; no request-derived value reaches titleKey, label (page integers), or icon (literals). The same literal-parameter pattern exists at fragments/layout.html:31 `@{__${link}__}`.

Unescaped output: `grep -rn -F -e 'utext' src/main/resources/templates` returns nothing; the fragment label renders through escaped inlining `[[${label}]]`. The fragment is not reachable as a view by request: view names are controller constants (VetController returns `vets/vetList`).

Injection into data access unchanged from round 1: the Specialty is bound as a parameter of the derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable)` and `(String)` in VetRepository.java; IgnoreCase on equality is not a LIKE match, so no wildcard injection.
Resource growth: the narrowed reads carry no `@Cacheable` (VetRepository.java diff), so caller-chosen values add nothing to the unbounded `vets` cache.

Input validation: `specialty` is an optional String @RequestParam, blank treated as absent via `StringUtils::hasText` (VetController.presentSpecialty); no request-bound object, no binder, no removed or weakened check in the diff.

Secrets: `python3 scripts/changeset.py | grep -i -E '^\+.*(password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential)'` matches only the docs/system-design.md inputs line mentioning environment-supplied datasource credentials, which adds no value.

Supply chain: `git status --short build.gradle gradle/ settings.gradle` is empty, so dependencies are unchanged from round 1 (Spring Boot 4.1.2, tools.jackson databind 3.1.7, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE per that pass's `./gradlew dependencies`); no NVD scan ran, a standing gap listed in docs/security-principles.md § Standing Gaps.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty in the address

blast_radius.note: Production reach is the vet package only: one optional request parameter on the two existing vet routes, two uncached derived queries on VetRepository, and a pagination-link fragment extracted from vetList.html. The four doc files record the decisions the owner made at intake (NG-9 narrowed, /vets reinstated, new ADR). No sensitive paths and no build or dependency changes.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk. With no specialty, both routes still call the same findAll reads, and the cached findAll(Pageable) is untouched. Blank input becomes absent through hasText, and the narrowed reads are equality-ignore-case derived queries, not LIKE. The fragment builds hrefs with link-expression parameters, so the value is URL-encoded. Its one preprocessing site, #{__${titleKey}__}, takes only template literals. It expands to an empty key for numbered links, but the ternary discards that, and the green page-link tests exercise it.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes against seeded H2. The repository case table covers whole name, upper case, prefix, unheld name, and 'none'. Listing tests check exact last names with full specialty sets, which proves distinct rows that keep all their specialties. The blank-input tests cover both routes. The page-link test asserts exact encoded hrefs for 'oral & dental'. One gap: the case table runs only the Collection overload, and the paged overload is checked with a lowercase name only.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved in the round-2 fix pass, but two approvals carry recommendations. The test-reviewer says bullet 5 (empty result gives 200) is tested only at the repository, not through either route. It says bullet 7 runs one page against the real database, and five declared test names drifted from the prd-entry. The code-quality-reviewer notes that pageLink.html reads specialty from the model implicitly instead of taking it as a parameter. Each claim is evidenced and none blocks.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake-decision: a URL contract only with no page control, both surfaces narrowed, pagination links carrying the parameter, NG-9 narrowed through a non-goal ADR, and /vets reinstated under a fresh id. The fix-round delta only refactored the template into a fragment and consolidated the blank check, with no new rule and no new route. No retries, consultations, or design revisions.

rationale: The code reads as safe and on-scope. The decisive point is the residual test gaps that reviewers parked as round-2 recommendations: empty-result 200 is untested at the web layer, and the paged overload's case-insensitivity is untested. Read VetController.java and pageLink.html, then decide whether those gaps are acceptable before merging.
